name: Sentry
summary: Sentry is an error monitoring service that catches crashes and bugs in your app and alerts you, with session replay and uptime checks built in.

free_plan_covers.note: The free Developer plan includes 5,000 errors, 50 session replays and 1 uptime monitor a month, for 1 user.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Team plan costs $29/month billed monthly (or $26/month billed yearly) for 50,000 errors a month and unlimited team members.

portability.note: Sentry's SDK is proprietary, but Sentry can also ingest OpenTelemetry traces and logs directly over OTLP, so existing OpenTelemetry instrumentation doesn't have to be replaced.

uptime_checks.note: Uptime Monitoring pings a URL you add on a schedule as often as every minute and alerts you when it fails; the free plan includes 1 monitor.

session_replay.note: Session Replay records what a person did before an error, and masks all text, form inputs and images by default so personal data never leaves the browser.

setup.step: Create a free Sentry account and a new project for your Next.js app.
Run the install wizard with npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs, and choose Error Monitoring, Tracing and Session Replay when it asks.
The wizard writes SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN to .env.sentry-build-plugin (already gitignored) for uploading source maps, and sets your DSN for the client to report to.
Start your dev server and open /sentry-example-page to trigger a test error, then confirm it shows up in Sentry.

builder_notes: Keep SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN out of client code and version control; it only belongs in the build environment for uploading source maps, unlike the DSN which is safe to ship to the browser.
Leave the wizard's withSentryConfig wrapper on next.config.ts so source maps upload automatically on every build, or stack traces will show minified code instead of your own.
Session replay masks all text, inputs and media by default; only turn that off for parts of the app you're sure never show personal data.
